scenes.title: SLAs, SLOs & SLIs for Data
scenes.subtitle: Measuring and promising data reliability
scenes.narration: SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs form a hierarchy for measuring data reliability, setting internal targets, and making external promises.

scenes.heading: The three terms
bullets: SLI: a measured indicator, like freshness lag
SLO: an internal target for that indicator
SLA: an external promise with consequences
Error budget: the allowed room to miss the SLO
scenes.narration: An SLI is a concrete measurement such as freshness lag or completeness percentage. An SLO is the internal target you hold that indicator to, like ninety-nine percent freshness. An SLA is a formal external promise that carries consequences if broken, and the error budget quantifies how much you may miss the SLO before you must act.

scenes.heading: From indicator to promise
steps: Choose an SLI that reflects user experience
Track performance against the error budget
Formalize the strongest ones as SLAs
scenes.narration: You start by choosing SLIs that genuinely reflect how consumers experience the data. You then set SLO targets that are ambitious yet achievable, and you track actual performance against the resulting error budget. Only the commitments you can reliably meet should be formalized into external SLAs.

scenes.heading: SLO versus SLA
scenes.narration: An SLO is an internal goal that guides where the team invests reliability effort, with no external penalty for a miss. An SLA is a contractual promise made to consumers, and breaching it carries real consequences such as credits or escalations. Teams typically set SLOs stricter than their SLAs to keep a safety margin.

scenes.heading: Computing a freshness SLI
scenes.code:
-- SLI: percent of the last 30 loads within the 1h freshness target
WITH loads AS (
  SELECT load_time,
         DATEDIFF('minute', event_max_ts, load_time) AS lag_min
  FROM load_audit
  ORDER BY load_time DESC
  LIMIT 30
)
SELECT
  AVG(CASE WHEN lag_min <= 60 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS freshness_sli
FROM loads;
scenes.narration: This query looks at the last thirty loads recorded in an audit table and computes each load's freshness lag in minutes. It then measures the fraction of those loads that met the one-hour target. That fraction is the freshness SLI, which you compare directly against your SLO to see whether you are inside the error budget.

scenes.text: Measure SLIs, target with SLOs, promise with SLAs, and let the error budget decide when to invest in reliability.
scenes.narration: This hierarchy turns reliability into numbers everyone can align on. The error budget is the key discipline, telling you objectively when to slow down and fix versus keep shipping.
